title: Dynamic commitment bands + deferred uplift credits | Renewal anchor & SQ sync
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Context: Large enterprise deals increasingly request both predictable committed spend and flexibility for expansion. Current renewal mechanics (single annual true-up + flat uplift %) creates awkward negotiations: customers either over-commit to avoid large mid-year true-ups or accept expensive uplift bands. We propose a new Renewal Anchor framework that combines dynamic commitment bands with deferred uplift credits and a staggered true-up window, and which ties checkpoint thresholds to Security Questionnaire (SQ) completion status to reduce procurement friction.

Proposal summary:
- Commitment bands: customers pick a baseline annual commitment band (e.g., Band A: 0-250k, Band B: 250k-1M, Band C: 1M+). Each band has a defined per-unit unit price and a refundable uplift credit schedule for mid-year expansion.
- Deferred uplift credits: when a customer expands usage mid-contract, they are issued a deferred uplift credit equal to a percentage of the overage (credited against next quarter invoices) rather than an immediate higher uplift rate. Credits vest over two subsequent billing cycles to avoid revenue accounting surprises.
- Staggered true-up windows: instead of one annual true-up, we offer two optional staggered windows (Q2 and Q4) where true-ups are reconciled, reducing quarter-end spikes.
- SQ sync gating: customers who have completed the latest Security Questionnaire (or a signed SOC/ISO attestation) unlock a lower uplift rate and accelerated credit vesting. This creates a commercial incentive to complete security due diligence early.

Why this helps:
- Reduces sticker shock and negotiation friction at renewal by smoothing expansion economics.
- Provides predictable accounting treatment for both Redwood and customers (credits vs retroactive rate changes).
- Encourages customers to finish security reviews earlier by embedding commercial benefits.

Success metrics (provisional):
- Increase net retention for pilot cohort by +4–8% y/y vs control.
- Reduce average mid-contract true-up size by 30% for participating accounts.
- Reduce procurement time-to-sign by 20% for deals where SQ sync incentive is used.

Scope & constraints:
- Pilot limited to mid-market and enterprise deals (>= $250k ARR) that commit to a 12–36 month term. Not available for pay-as-you-go accounts in hosted API tier.
- Requires billing platform changes to track deferred credits and apply vesting schedule; needs accounting sign-off on revenue recognition.
- Requires Console UI changes to display band, credit balance, vesting schedule, and SQ status.

Stakeholders: Finance (revenue recognition), Legal (contract language for credits), Sales (pricing playbooks), Solutions Engineering (SQ questionnaire integration), Engineering (billing & console), Customer Success (pilot selection).
acceptance_criteria: Pilot pricing rubric documented and approved by Finance and Legal
Billing system supports deferred uplift credits and two-cycle vesting (test coverage + runbook)
Console shows commitment band, live credit balance, vesting timeline, and SQ completion link
Sales playbook and templated contract clause created and distributed to AE pilots
Pilot launched with at least 10 qualified enterprise accounts and first true-up window executed without manual adjustments
implementation_notes: Billing tasks: add Credit ledger table, API endpoints to issue/apply credits, and end-of-cycle reconciliation job
Console tasks: add band selection in renewal flow, credit balance widget, and SQ status badge pulled from Security Portal API
Legal to draft clause: 'Deferred uplift credit' definition, vesting mechanics, termination handling
Finance to confirm revenue recognition treatment (ASC 606 implications) and monthly close checklist updates
Sales enablement: one-pager, objection handling FAQ, pricing examples for 12/24/36 month terms
risks: Accounting complexity could delay launch if ASC 606 treatment requires amortization adjustments
Sales may over-complicate deals; need strict playbook to avoid custom one-off credits
If SQ linkage creates perception of gatekeeping, some customers may slow down procurement
Engineering backlog risk: billing and console work may compete with high-priority runtime initiatives
